dream.title: Dream · The anthill
pages:
I am on that road again. Father holds his car keys. Mother turns away.

I shout something. Neither looks back.

An anthill beside my shoe. An ant drags a white husk, stuck at the entrance.

I crouch down. The argument continues behind me.

I kick it.

Wet soil sticks to my shoe. Ants crawl onto my sock. I stamp my foot.

The light goes.

A shadow covers the road. Covers both of them.

When I wake, my toes are still curled under the blanket.
dream.journalBody:
The road. My parents arguing. I kicked an anthill.
Then a shadow covered them both. I woke with my feet curled up.
dream.fallbackPage: I woke from a dream about an anthill.

knowledge.ancientBody:
The stars bent along its edge.
I took my eye away before I could find the other end.
knowledge.windowBody: Something has changed between the buildings. I wrote down what I could see.

telescope.title: Telescope
telescope.nightOnly:
Glare fills the lens.
Come back after sunset.
telescope.wrongDay:
I turn the focus ring. Rooftops and stars.
Nothing else tonight.
telescope.gainedSuffix: My hand is shaking. Can I still draw the edge?
telescope.repeatSuffix: That edge again. I could try drawing it.

firstLoop.news:
SKT-079 is expected to sweep past Earth. Some disruption to electronic signals is anticipated. Monitoring continues.

The voice warps. A line cuts across the screen.

I look towards the balcony. The telescope is where I left it.
firstLoop.flyer:
COVER YOUR WINDOWS.
Do not trust the calm voices.
Something is coming from above.
firstLoop.dayOneCaption: The man from 401 presses a flyer against the wall. His lips keep moving.
firstLoop.startledCaption:
He sees me.
The tape sticks to his finger. He pulls it free and runs inside.
firstLoop.boardingCaption:
Another nail. Another board.
He does not answer.
firstLoop.chapterText:
I take my eye away.

The balcony is still here. So is the building opposite.

I do not touch the focus ring again.
firstLoop.newsDay1:
Static. The screen flashes, then goes dark.
The power light stays on.
firstLoop.newsDefault: News between bursts of static. Nothing new.

dayOneBroadcast.title: EMERGENCY BROADCAST
dayOneBroadcast.lateFirstPage:
The television is still on.
The noon bulletin is repeating.
pages:
The television comes on. The remote is still under the magazine.

White first. Then a newsreader.

“We interrupt this programme. Supernova pulse SKT-079 has entered monitoring range.”

His lips keep moving after the sound stops.

“Expected within seven days. Remain indoors. Cover your windows.”

“Repeat. Cover your windows.”

A different voice says the last three words.

A star field.

The clock in the corner has stopped.

One star goes out. Comes back.

I touch the power button.

Two soft taps from inside the glass.

I pull my hand back.

The screen goes black.

My reflection stands there.

I take a step to the side.
dayOneBroadcast.journalBody:
The television switched itself on at noon. SKT-079, seven days. Stay inside. Cover the windows.
A star blinked on the screen. Two taps came from the glass.

bedroom.title: Writing in the margin
bedroom.body:
Old scratches at the desk edge.
“Not stars moving. Its eyes.”
The grooves catch under my nail.

corridor.title: Beneath the flyer
corridor.body:
Writing beneath the wallpaper.
“Boards will not stop it. I just do not want to see.”
Why could I not read this before?

balcony.title: Marks on the railing
balcony.body:
Seven shallow cuts. The last crosses the others.
Below them: “Stop counting.”

evidence.title: My observation book
evidence.body:
Months of star positions, cloud cover and times. A note: half a turn on the focus ring; balcony light off first.
My handwriting. The dates have gaps, but the notes keep going.

evidence.title: The balcony telescope
evidence.body: A polished focus ring. A north mark beside the tripod. My calibration marks on the tube match the book.

evidence.title: The flyer from 401
evidence.body:
COVER YOUR WINDOWS. Do not trust the calm voices. Something is coming from above.
Fresh paper. Tape still tacky at the corners.

evidence.title: 401 boarded shut
evidence.body:
Day two. Fresh boards over the door. Even the gaps are covered.
He did not answer me.

evidence.title: SKT-079 news extract
evidence.body:
Day two: SKT-079 may disrupt electronic signals. The voice warps halfway through.
No mention of anything alive.

evidence.title: The outline · A memory sketch
evidence.body:
Second night. A shape through the telescope. I drew what I remembered. Stars bent around the edge.
A memory, not a photograph. I have no second observation.

evidence.title: The view on day two
evidence.body: The skyline looks different today. I recorded the view. No measurements to compare.

evidence.title: Writing in the margin
evidence.body:
Old writing at the desk edge: “Not stars moving. Its eyes.”
I could only read it when I was unwell.

evidence.title: Beneath the flyer
evidence.body:
Beneath the wallpaper: “Boards will not stop it. I just do not want to see.”
I do not know who wrote it.

evidence.title: Marks on the railing
evidence.body:
Seven shallow cuts. The last crosses the others. “Stop counting.”
No name. No date.

evidence.title: Tank label
evidence.body:
Water changes: Sundays. The last tick is in my handwriting.
The pump cable crosses the paper. There is no crease beneath it.

evidence.title: An eye behind the glass
evidence.body:
Day three. An eye pressed against the inside of the glass.
It did not follow when I moved left. When I turned away, a voice said: Quietly.

evidence.title: The old waterline
evidence.body:
Day five. A dry tide mark crosses the cabinet, above the hand resting on the tank.
The wood above it is dry.

evidence.title: The name 001
evidence.body:
Day six. Outside the tank, it asked me to write down 001.
It said I hid my observation book badly. It never gave me a name.

evidence.title: Missing pages
evidence.body:
Two paper stubs remain in the binding. Saturday on either side.
The cloud cover, times, even the crossed-out number are identical.

evidence.title: Dust beneath 403
evidence.body:
A thin line of dust. No footprints.
A chair scraped across the floor inside. When I knocked, it stopped.

deductions.title: Astronomy is my hobby
deductions.body: Months of records match the worn telescope. I have been doing this for a while.

deductions.title: An observation through the telescope
deductions.body:
The sketch records a view through this telescope, not an image from the news.
It does not rule out a faulty lens or a faulty memory.

deductions.title: I chose to look
deductions.body:
I knew the instrument. I went looking.
That does not make what I saw reliable. I need another witness.

deductions.title: The warning came first
deductions.body:
The day-one flyer predates the day-two bulletin. Both mention the sky.
The noon broadcast also warned about windows. Did 401 hear something earlier still?

deductions.title: He followed his own warning
deductions.body:
He told people to cover windows. Then he covered his own door.
I still do not know what frightened him.

deductions.title: Perhaps he did not want to see
deductions.body:
The writing fits the covered gaps. He may be avoiding the sight of something.
I do not know who wrote it.

deductions.title: Something in my tank
deductions.body:
I maintained this tank. Something in it now speaks.
The label says nothing about it. It does not tell me when it arrived.

deductions.title: Before it left the tank
deductions.body:
The day-five waterline was higher than its exposed hand. On day six it stood outside.
It may have climbed out earlier. The stain could also be older.

deductions.title: Another reader
deductions.body:
001 knows about the book. Pages have been torn out.
I should ask about them. Knowing the book exists does not make it responsible.

aquarium.promptDay3: E  Speak to the thing in the tank
day3Pages: The filter hums. An eye presses against the glass.

“Quietly.”

I have not touched the tank.

“You asked yesterday.”

A few bubbles reach the surface.
day5Pages: A hand rests on the rim. Water runs over the extension lead. The power light is still on.

“Move that.”

It points beside the cabinet.

I ask where it came from.

“Bring a towel first.”
The old waterline is higher than its hand.
day6Pages:
The tank is empty.

It stands beside the cabinet. No water under its feet.
“You do not hide that book very well.”

I ask how many times it has read it.

It watches me. It does not count.
aquarium.question: Ask: Have you read my book?
aquarium.answerGap:
It holds up two fingers.

“You only found two pages?”
